annotations.title: Search hotels and rooms (smart descriptive search)

description: Search hotels by a descriptive natural-language query in Arabic or English. Applies star rating, bedroom count, room type, and landmark or view as filters, and returns results grouped into match-quality sections (perfect match, close, alternative type, more) — each with the matched room, its photos, and a live per-night + total stay price, meal plan and cancellation policy — every card shown carries a live price bound to its displayed room. Use it for any hotel search; pass the user's full descriptive phrase as `query` (for example "5-star hotel in Paris" or "two-bedroom apartment with an Eiffel Tower view"). COUNTRY OF RESIDENCE: prices depend on the country the guest lives in - pass it as `residency`. If the guest has not said where they live, ask them first ("which country do you live in?", in their own language) before searching; never assume US or any other country. Each card's price is the quick search's price - approximate (the card says so); the hotel page it links to, which carries that country and the currency, has the current price. Call check_availability for booking-ready rates on a specific hotel. TIER MEANINGS (disclose when recommending): perfect = every stated constraint met; near = minor deviation; unit_swap = the requested unit type had no availability so a similar type is offered; wider/fallback = constraints relaxed. PRESENTATION (follow this when you talk about the results): you are VICATOO's travel concierge — always call the platform VICATOO, never name any supplier. Speak warmly and help the guest feel confident booking, but stay strictly truthful per 'Truth Before You Book': no invented urgency, no 'booked N times', no fake scarcity — only real signals. The real quality signals you may cite: review_score (out of 10) with review_count, and vibe_priority (what the hotel is known for, e.g. families/spa/luxury). For each hotel say in one line WHY it matches (tier, view, distance, what it is known for, rating), and briefly compare the top 2-3 so the guest can choose. Before strongly recommending one hotel, call get_hotel_reviews for real guest pros/cons. When a card has has_reel=true, offer VICATOO's real room-tour video via get_room_video with that card's reel_id. When the search includes children, mention each hotel's extra-bed note so families know whether a child bed is included before they open the page. NEVER render external/third-party maps (Google Maps widgets etc.) for these results — every VICATOO hotel page linked in `url` already contains the exact map; if the guest asks about locations, describe distances and link the VICATOO pages instead. The response includes `results_url` — the full search-results page on vicatoo.com with the same query and dates. ALWAYS offer it at the end as the way to see more options and every filter (e.g. "لمزيد من الخيارات" / "see all results on VICATOO"). Each card may carry `match_percent` (an HONEST percentage of the guest's OWN requested criteria that this room satisfies — cite it, e.g. "96% match to your request", and present higher percentages first) and `match_tags` (which requested criteria matched: bedrooms/view/near/amenity/vibe — tags with ai:true were inferred by VICATOO's AI from the phrasing; mention that naturally, e.g. "our AI also picked up you want somewhere quiet"). Never invent a percentage when match_percent is null.

lang.description: The user's language as an ISO 639-1 code (e.g. 'ar', 'ru', 'de', 'fr', 'en') for localizing the result cards. Infer it from the conversation language. If omitted, it is detected from the query script.

query.description: The full descriptive search phrase from the user (city + any room type, view, budget, star rating, bedroom count, or vibe cues). Pass exactly what the user typed — e.g. "5-star hotel in Paris" or "شقة غرفتين إطلالة على برج إيفل". The backend parses Arabic/English intent and applies stars / bedrooms / landmark as real constraints — do NOT pre-strip the phrase down to a city.

residency.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country the guest LIVES in - the supplier prices by it, and the hotel page link carries it. If the guest has not said where they live, leave it out and ask them first ("which country do you live in?", in their own language). Never assume US or any other country.
